newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seeks wide tariff cuts, not only on paper.
newsitem.headline: EU seeks wide tariff cuts, not only on paper.

text.p: European Union Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan told U.S. forest industry representatives on Thursday he favoured faster tariff cuts, but not only in one sector such as the paper and wood industry.
"It is not possible to entertain the idea of cutting tariffs in one sector without cutting them in others," his spokesman Peter Guilford told Reuters.

Brittan met with representatives of the American Forest & Paper Association (AF&PA), which is pressing for action to accelerate cuts in EU tariffs on forestry products, which it says are much higher than those in the United States.

The AF&PA wants the tariffs to end as soon as possible and not in 2004 which was agreed in the Uruguay Round trade pact in 1994. According to AF&PA, some European tariffs are still at seven percent while most paper products enter the United States duty free.

"They asked our views about cutting tariffs in paper and wood products and we said that we favour a new trade liberalisation round," Guilford said, adding the Commission was seeking an acceleration of tariff cuts across the board.
"We say we are in favour of tariff acceleration but it has got to be a balanced negotiation."
For example, EU producers had real problems getting into the U.S. textile, glass and ceramics markets becuase of high tariffs, he said.
"Now U.S. producers want us to cut tariffs on wood, fair enough, but a trade round is all about negotiations and we want it to be as widespread as possible," he added.
The Confederation of European Paper Industries (CEPI) last year rejected calls from the U.S. forest industry for faster tariff cuts on newsprint and other paper products.
